time.
Software can help you implement models, but can't tell you which model
might in principle be worth considering (until after you've tried
them).
You need to provide the specifics of the model you wish to implement.
What such a model might look like is a research question specific to
your context, and not a software question.

Finn

The number of models that can be implemented is virtually infinite,
and explaining all of them, or even list a subset would take too much
time.
Software can help you implement models, but can't tell you which model
might in principle be worth considering (until after you've tried
them).
You need to provide the specifics of the model you wish to implement.
What such a model might look like is a research question specific to
your context, and not a software question.
